title: Project, project management and business as usual
blurb: Define a project and project management, and use the five characteristics to tell a project from business as usual.
question: A team will run for eight months, bring together staff from three departments and hand a new booking system over to operations. Which characteristics show this is a project rather than business as usual?

teach.h: Three terms the exam expects you to know
teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile builds on PRINCE2 Project Management, so it starts with three key terms: project, project management and performance target. A project is a temporary organization set up to deliver one or more products according to an agreed business case. Project management is how that organization is run. A performance target sets the level of success the project is judged against (the next lesson covers the seven targets).

head: Term
In plain English
rows: A temporary team set up to deliver agreed products, justified by a business case
Using methods, tools, techniques and skills so the project meets its objectives
The ongoing, repetitive work that keeps the organization running
teach.caption: Definitions paraphrased from 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 of the PRINCE2 Agile V2 book.

teach.body: Project management is the application of methods, tools, techniques and competencies so that the project meets its objectives. Notice it is not just a method on paper: it includes the people skills needed to apply it. In PRINCE2 Agile this means PRINCE2 direction and management working alongside agile delivery teams.

rows.label: Temporary
values: Has a start and an end

teach.caption: The first four are quoted in the Agile book 1.3.1; uncertainty is the fifth in PRINCE2 7.

steps.label: Products handed over
steps.sub: at the end of the project

teach.caption: BAU identifies the need; the project is the means of introducing it.

children.edge: start and end, then BAU takes over
children.label: Temporary

teach.body: Fenwick Valley Health's outpatients department books appointments every day: that is business as usual. Its managers identify a need for online self-booking. Project manager Grace Okafor leads an eight-month project with IT, clinical and finance staff (cross-functional) that has never been done in this trust before (unique). When the system goes live, the outpatients team runs it as BAU and the project closes (temporary). The project introduced the change; BAU keeps it going.

teach.text: 'Unique' and 'temporary' are the classic mix-up. Temporary is about the project having a start and an end, after which BAU adopts the change. Unique is about each project differing in team, customer, supplier, product, location or timeframe, even if similar projects have gone before.

items: Project: a temporary organization delivering products according to an agreed business case.
Project management: methods, tools, techniques and competencies applied so the project meets its objectives.
Five characteristics: change, temporary, cross-functional, unique and uncertainty.
BAU identifies the need for change; the project introduces it; BAU then adopts it.

summary: You can now define a project, project management and business as usual in the PRINCE2 Agile sense. You can also name the characteristic shown in a short description, especially telling temporary from unique.

A.q: Which statement best defines a project in PRINCE2 Project Management?
options: An ongoing team that runs and improves a product after it goes live
A temporary organization delivering products to an agreed business case
A permanent function that improves the organization's processes yearly
A series of iterations that a delivery team plans and runs for itself
A.why: A project is a temporary organization created to deliver one or more products according to an agreed business case (1.3.1).

whyNot.0: Running a product after go-live is business as usual, not a project.
whyNot.2: A project is temporary, not a permanent function.
whyNot.3: Iterations are timeboxes used by delivery teams; they are not the definition of a project.

A.q: What is project management, as described in PRINCE2 Agile?
options: Applying methods, tools, techniques and competencies so a project meets its objectives
Recording the products that operational teams maintain once a project has closed
Setting the strategy of the organization that sponsors a portfolio of projects
Running the daily stand-up and retrospective events of each delivery team
A.why: Project management is the application of methods, tools, techniques and competencies to enable the project to meet its objectives (1.3.2).

whyNot.1: Maintaining products after closure is a business as usual activity.
whyNot.2: Organizational strategy is set by the business, above the project.
whyNot.3: Team events are part of agile delivery, not the definition of project management.

A.q: A project has a defined start and end, after which business as usual adopts the change and its benefits. Which characteristic of a project is this?
A.why: Temporary means a project has a start and an end, after which BAU adopts the resulting change (1.3.1).

whyNot.0: Unique is about each project differing in team, customer, location or timeframe.
whyNot.1: Change is about the project introducing what BAU has identified as needed.
whyNot.3: Cross-functional is about teams working across divisions or organizations.

B.q: A retailer has opened many stores, but each new store project has a different site, contractor and local team. Which project characteristic does this illustrate?
B.why: Unique means projects differ from each other, for example in team, customer, supplier, location or timeframe (1.3.1).

whyNot.0: Temporary is about the project having a start and an end.
whyNot.1: Cross-functional is about people from several divisions working together.
whyNot.2: Change is about the project introducing what BAU needs.

B.q: Which describes how business as usual and projects relate to change?
options: Projects identify the need for change and BAU introduces it
BAU identifies the need for change and projects introduce it
BAU and projects both introduce change in the same way
Projects introduce change and then continue as BAU teams
B.why: BAU identifies a need for change; projects are the means by which the change is introduced (1.3.1).

whyNot.2: BAU is ongoing and repetitive; introducing change is the role of a project.
whyNot.3: Projects are temporary: they close and BAU adopts the change.

B.q: A council project brings together planners, IT staff and an external software supplier. Which project characteristic is shown?
B.why: Cross-functional means project teams work across functional divisions and sometimes span organizations (1.3.1).

whyNot.1: Temporary concerns the start and end of the project, not who is in it.
whyNot.2: Unique concerns how the project differs from others.
whyNot.3: Change concerns introducing what BAU needs.

C.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. A project is created to deliver products according to an agreed business case.
2. Business as usual is temporary and ends when the change is complete.
3. Project management includes the competencies needed to apply methods and tools.
4. A project continues after handover to run the products it delivered.
C.why: Statement 1 matches the project definition (1.3.1) and statement 3 matches project management: methods, tools, techniques and competencies (1.3.2).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: BAU is ongoing; the project is the temporary part.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: BAU is ongoing and a project closes after handover.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: after handover, BAU runs the products.

C.q: A charity's helpline answers calls daily. It now sets up an eight-month team, drawn from three departments, to introduce a new case-management system. Which pairing is correct?
options: Helpline is a project; new system work is BAU
Both are BAU because the charity runs them
Helpline is BAU; new system work is a project
Both are projects because both use teams
C.why: The daily helpline is ongoing and repetitive (BAU). The system work is temporary, cross-functional and introduces change, so it is a project (1.3.1).

whyNot.0: This reverses them: the helpline is the ongoing work.
whyNot.1: The system work has a start and end and introduces change, so it is a project.
whyNot.3: Having a team does not make ongoing helpline work a project.

C.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. A project is a [?] organization created to deliver one or more products according to an agreed business case.
C.why: The project definition describes a temporary organization; once the change is introduced, the project closes (1.3.1).

whyNot.0: Projects are cross-functional, working across functional divisions.
whyNot.1: Projects end; BAU is the ongoing, permanent work.
whyNot.2: Standalone is an organizational context (versus a programme), not the definition.

reteach.title: The kitchen and the refit
reteach.question: Why is refitting a restaurant kitchen a project when cooking every night is not?

blocks.h: Cooking is BAU; the refit is a project
blocks.body: Cooking every night is repetitive and ongoing: business as usual. The kitchen refit has a start and an end (temporary), brings in builders, electricians and chefs (cross-functional), is unlike any other refit (unique), introduces change and carries more uncertainty. When it ends, the kitchen goes back to cooking in its new form.

blocks.text: Ask two questions: does the work end once the change is in place, and does it introduce something new? If yes to both, it is a project.

explain.body: A project is a temporary organization created to deliver one or more products according to an agreed business case (1.3.1). The business case is what justifies it.

test.q: According to the project definition, what must a project's products be delivered in line with?
test.why: A project delivers products according to an agreed business case (1.3.1).

whyNot.0: The Definition of Done is a quality tool used by teams, not part of the project definition.
whyNot.1: The annual budget is a BAU planning tool, not what the definition names.
whyNot.3: Supplier contracts sit in the commercial context; the definition names the business case.

explain.body: Applying methods, tools, techniques and competencies so the project meets its objectives (1.3.2). Competencies matter as much as the method.

test.q: Which item is part of the description of project management in PRINCE2 Agile?
test.why: Project management applies methods, tools, techniques and competencies (1.3.2).

whyNot.1: Contracts belong to the commercial context, not the definition.
whyNot.2: Portfolios are an organizational context a project may sit in.
whyNot.3: Iterations are delivery timeboxes, not part of the definition.

explain.body: Temporary: a start and an end, after which BAU adopts the change. Unique: different team, customer, supplier, product, location or timeframe (1.3.1).

test.q: A hospital's new ward project closes once the ward opens, and ward staff then run it. Which characteristic does this show?
test.why: The project ends and BAU takes over the change: that is temporary (1.3.1).

whyNot.0: Unique would be shown by differences from other projects.
whyNot.1: Cross-functional would be shown by staff from several divisions.
whyNot.2: Change is the project introducing what BAU needs, not the project ending.

explain.body: BAU identifies a need for change; the project is the means of introducing it. Uncertainty follows: projects carry more threats and opportunities than BAU.

test.q: Which characteristic says that projects are the means by which a need identified in BAU is introduced?
test.why: Change: BAU identifies the need for change, and projects are the means of introducing it (1.3.1).

whyNot.0: Temporary is about the start and end of a project.
whyNot.2: Unique is about how each project differs from others.
whyNot.3: Cross-functional is about teams spanning divisions.
